item.description: Three of Team Teppen’s brightest kickboxing talents are locked in and ready to make a statement on home soil. Japanese stars Ryujin “SHINDO” Nasukawa , Masashi “The Flash” Kumura , and “Mr. No Damage” Gump took part in an open workout at the Team Teppen gym last week, showing off their skills ahead of ONE SAMURAI 5 . All three are currently scheduled for action on the card, which broadcasts live from EBARA WAVE Arena Ota in Tokyo, Japan, on Wednesday, November 18. Photo Credit: ONE Championship Ryujin: Bigger Goals In Sight The 20-year-old Ryujin, who is the younger brother of legendary kickboxing megastar Tenshin Nasukawa, will face Elmehdi “The Sniper” El Jamari in a strawweight kickboxing clash. Introduced to martial arts by his father, the ISKA World Champion holds a 20-3 career record and made a statement in his ONE Championship debut at The Inner Circle 23 in July, where he knocked out Thai veteran Thongpoon PK Saenchai . Now he has his sights set even higher, with future plans to challenge for the ONE Atomweight Muay Thai World Title, which is currently held by his compatriot, Nadaka Yoshinari . Asked about the atomweight king, Ryujin said he feels people are overlooking him: “I don’t know, but I kind of feel like I’m being underestimated somewhere. There’s a part of me that’s thinking, ‘Don’t look down on me.’ But I’m not in a position to say anything yet, so I want to keep that feeling with me as I head into my fight in ONE.” View this post on Instagram Kumura: Ready For The Global Stage Kumura makes his ONE Championship debut against former ONE Strawweight Muay Thai World Title challenger “El Jefe” Ellis Badr Barboza in another strawweight kickboxing matchup. The 27-year-old Osaka native started his martial arts journey with karate and turned pro in kickboxing at the age of 15. He enters the contest with a 26-8 career record and has a chance to send a strong message to the entire division with a victory over a former contender. Kumura said: “Barboza has already fought for a Muay Thai title in ONE, so there is no doubt he is one of ONE’s top fighters. If I can beat a fighter like that in a convincing way, it will raise my stock. I want to win without taking any damage.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Gump: Riding The Momentum Rounding out the trio, the 23-year-old Gump meets Shuto “Atomic Bomb” Inui in an all-Japanese bantamweight kickboxing showdown. Gump is 19-5 overall and 2-0 in ONE Championship, with both promotional victories coming by decision. He aims to extend that run to three straight wins and believes his recent experience on the organization’s weekly Asia primetime event series has given him an edge. item.title: LSU flips linebacker Ja'Marquis Hudson away from Kansas
item.description: Ja’Marquis Hudson is from Louisiana. His mother was set to attend LSU — before beginning her family and ultimately moving to Texas. LSU has been a force in Hudson’s recruitment during a fantastic senior season at Port Arthur (Texas) Memorial . After a second visit back to Baton Rouge, Hudson flipped his commitment from Kansas to the Tigers. “LSU has been watching my senior season and I’m excited about being back in my home state,” Hudson told Rivals. “I’ve been watching LSU since I was a kid, and all of my family are naturally big fans of the Tigers being from Louisiana, so it’s just great ties and it fits perfectly.” “The culture and how dedicated everyone is to participating in the culture … I feel football teams feed off stuff like that as motivation,” he added after his official visit over the weekend. Hudson was in Baton Rouge last month when LSU hosted Mississippi State. He returned over the weekend for an official viist — and the Tigers have been trending up in this recruitment ever since. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound linebacker also sees snaps at nickel. He is a gifted track athlete as well, out in Southeast Texas. Hudson ranks as the No. 580 overall prospect in the 2027 class, per the Rivals Industry Rankings. He is the No. 44 linebacker and the No. 73 player in the state of Texas — regardless of position.

item.title: Tank Dell is back: Houston Texans receiver scores first TD in nearly two years after scary injury
item.description: Houston Texans wide receiver Tank Dell (1) makes a touchdown catch past Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson (26) during the first half of an NFL football game in Inglewood, Calif., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill) (Mark J. Terrill/Associated Press) C.J. Stroud and Tank Dell were doing the Squabble on Sunday like it was 2024. In the Houston Texans' game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium, Dell scored his first touchdown since Dec. 21, 2024, a span of 687 days. The last time Dell had scored came on the same day he suffered a catastrophic injury that resulted in multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap. The Texans receiver missed nearly two full years with the injury before finally returning in the loss to the New York Giants two weeks ago. He found paydirt in his second game back. On a second down from the Texans' 37, Stroud dropped back and looked Dell's way. Dell was covered tightly by Donte Jackson, but Stroud dropped it over the cornerback's outstretched arms, Dell hauled in the perfectly thrown ball and was off to the races for a 63-yard touchdown that put the Texans up 17-9. item.description: Ryan Day was asked at his postgame news conference Saturday night where the Ohio State Buckeyes go from here, with a 41-28 home loss to the Oregon Ducks having just handed him the first three-loss season of his eight years in charge. The question noted that a Big Ten title and a College Football Playoff berth now look like long shots, and Day accepted the premise. “Not someplace we thought we’d be. Beyond disappointed. We understand what the expectations are. It’s the like first thing when you walk into the Woody, you join our program, you understand what the expectations are. The expectation is to win every game here. To lose three games is unacceptable, and I own that. That’s never going to change from my point of view… Now we got to weather this storm, something that none of us are used to,” Day said. From there, it was a chaotic scene when a massive sea of people hopped onto the side of the ring, as well as inside, and started throwing objects and punches trying to get at the visitor. Aliev was eventually taken out of the ring, but that did not stop the fans from attacking him as he was hit by several more punches as well as a chair on his head. item.title: UAlbany men's basketball stumbles down stretch in loss to Merrimack
item.description: Erwann Bussing of UAlbany takes a shot in front of Dylan Veillette of Merrimack at the Broadview Center in Albany, NY on Sunday, November 8, 2026. Stephen Weaver/For the Times Union (Stephen Weaver) ALBANY - As quickly as the University at Albany men's basketball team clawed its way back from a 10-point second-half deficit to tie Sunday's game against Merrimack at Broadview Center, the Great Danes found themselves on the back foot once again. This time, they couldn't find their way out of the hole. Merrimack's vaunted zone defense forced UAlbany into 21 turnovers - 14 in the first half - and the Great Danes watched as the Warriors' A.J. Lesburt Jr. hit seven 3-pointers on his way to a game-high 25 points as Merrimack pulled away for a 73-60 win. The loss dropped UAlbany to 2-1 early in the season, as the Great Danes were unable to complete a sweep of their America East-Metro Basketball Challenge games after beating Manhattan on the road on Thursday. "To be honest with you, I wanted the whole week," UAlbany coach Dwayne Killings said. "That was our goal, to have a complete week. We did not." U-Mier Graham of UAlbany takes a shot in front of Elijah Wilborn of Merrimack at the Broadview Center in Albany, NY on Sunday, November 8, 2026. Stephen Weaver/For the Times Union (Stephen Weaver) Merrimack (1-2 overall) coach Joe Gallo's trademark zone has flummoxed plenty of opponents, and it gave the Great Danes trouble throughout Sunday's contest. UAlbany was often able to get the ball into the soft spot in the middle of the zone, but when the Warriors collapsed on the player with the ball - usually one of Ollie Engen, U-Mier Graham or Erwann Bussing - it resulted in problems the Great Danes were unable to solve. "It's their identity," Engen said of the Merrimack zone. "They practice it really well. They know each of the spots that they've got to be in, (they have) active hands. We've just got to be more assertive, more confident in our passing and take better advantage of it." "I thought the zone kind of sped us up," Killings said. "We weren't really fundamental there." Despite turning the ball over 14 times in the game's opening 20 minutes, UAlbany only trailed 30-26 at the half. item.title: Flag football championships: Las Lomas completes perfect season with NCS Division 2 title
item.description: Las Lomas senior wide receiver Violet Keeperman played a starring role in Saturday's 19-0 win over Carondelet in the North Coast Section Division 2 championship game. (Courtesy of Ernie Abrea/MaxPreps) As the ball sailed high into the Moraga night on Saturday, Las Lomas-Walnut Creek senior Violet Keeperman, sprinting all alone down the left sideline, said time stood still. All those drills, practices, and routes catching the ball from childhood bestie and Knights' quarterback Maggie Kruger were not going to be wasted. Not at this moment. Not in her final game, in the North Coast Section Division 2 championship game, with a perfect season on the line, a large, loud crowd in attendance and most important, her 19 teammates and four coaches - one being her beloved dad Matt, the defensive coordinator - counting on her. "It was like everything went silent," she said. "I tuned everything out. I was just completely focused on catching the ball, getting into the end zone and celebrating with my team." It all happened in one poetic instance. Keeperman, in perfect stride, hauled in the 50-yard pass early in the third quarter, sprinted to the back of end zone, twirled in the air, dropped to her knees, screamed to the skies before being mobbed by her teammates - a magic, celebratory moment of a 19-0 victory over Carondelet-Concord to punctuate a 24-0 season that washed away some of the sting from an NCS semifinal loss last year that spoiled what had been a 25-0 season. Kruger (24-for-32, 185 yards, three touchdowns) and Keeperman (five catches, 71 yards) connected again on the game's last TD, a 6-yarder in the fourth quarter that marked the 29th time they had teamed for a score this season and 49th time over the past two seasons. Kruger, whose dad Tim is the head coach, also threw a 2-yard TD pass to Hannah Shank (11 catches, 50 yards) and rushed for a game-high 77 yards. She finished with more than 3,700 passing yards and 1,700 rushing yards and 105 total touchdowns. Las Lomas was one of three NCS champions crowned at Campolindo on Saturday and four more won Central Coast Section titles at Los Gatos. The Chronicle's top-ranked team was the only one to finish unbeaten, making the Knights 49-1 over two seasons. "It's quite surreal we just did this," said Tim Kruger, whose first NCS title as a head coach came in his 32nd year coaching a variety of sports at Las Lomas. item.title: Legendary coach believes Shedeur Sanders ‘should be the starter’ for the Cleveland Browns after performance vs. Saints
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Bill Cowher has stated that he wants Shedeur Sanders to be the starter of the Cleveland Browns after the young quarterback’s performance against the New Orleans Saints. Despite the narrow 22-23 loss in overtime, Sanders threw for 297 yards and had two touchdowns during the game. After it was announced that Sanders would be starting with Deshaun Watson ruled out due to a concussion, there was a lot of excitement, as early in training camp, many thought Sanders was going to be the starter. However, coach Todd Monken went with experience and gave Watson the nod as the starter, and he has been impressive. But after watching Sanders play, coach Bill Cowher wants the Browns to give him the permanent job. “Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team. He’s gonna be the future. I think what he showed today was his resiliency; he continued to come back, he made great decisions, he extended plays, I loved the way he played and I would move forward with Shedeur Sanders,” said Cowher on CBS. Although the Browns lost the game, Sanders made some big plays that showed everyone how talented a player he is. In regulation, the Saints scored a touchdown to take a three-point lead with just 50 seconds left. Without showing any panic, Sanders made quick plays to take the ball within field goal range to tie the score. Then, in overtime, Sanders threw a touchdown pass and gave the Browns a chance to secure the game. They lost the game after a failed attempt to complete the two-point conversion. With Sanders having proven that he is ready to take over, coach Monken has a big decision to make. Playing Watson is a decision that has helped the Browns become a good team in the AFC North. He has displayed great performances, but the past is always going to be a problem when it comes to Watson. His injury history and off-the-field controversies makes it hard for the Browns to give him the next extension, which means Sanders will be the franchise QB. Allowing him to start in a few meaningful games is going to be important in his development, which is why Cowher’s take definitely makes sense.
